stem: A Massachusetts preceptor is reviewing a candidate's internship record against the Board-approved internship requirement. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: One pathway requires at least 1500 hours, of which at least 1000 are in a Board-approved pharmacy or pharmacy-related setting.
On that pathway at least 500 hours must be in clinical pharmacy, a demonstration project, manufacturing, or analytical or industrial pharmacy.
An alternative pathway is at least 1500 intern hours acquired through experiential pharmacy education for a graduate of an ACPE-accredited institution.
The Board may grant credit for out-of-state internship experience on appropriate documentation.
All 1500 hours must be acquired within a single calendar year.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 8.01(1) sets a 1500-hour requirement with a 1000-hour and 500-hour internal composition on the first pathway and an alternative 1500-hour experiential pathway for graduates of ACPE-accredited institutions. 247 CMR 8.01(11) allows credit for out-of-state experience on an affidavit or certificate from the jurisdiction where it was acquired, and 247 CMR 8.01(5) provides that hours may be acquired throughout a calendar year rather than compressed into one.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: the 1000-hour component sits inside the 1500-hour total.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: the 500-hour component names those four settings.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: the experiential pathway is an alternative for ACPE-accredited graduates.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: out-of-state experience is creditable on documentation.
choice_analysis.E: No single-calendar-year confinement is imposed; hours may be acquired throughout a calendar year.

related_facts: A pharmacy intern may not receive more than 12 hours of internship credit per day.
explanation.mpje_trap: The headline 1500 hours hides an internal composition that a raw hour count can satisfy without meeting.

reasoning_steps: Check the internal 1000-hour and 500-hour composition on the first pathway
Apply the documentation route for out-of-state experience
